section_summary: This section reproduces a varied portion of the April 1948 issue of World Youth. It concludes the Finnish adventure “One-Armed Sailor,” presents features on Aranmula metal mirrors and the atmosphere, prints readers’ letters and an animal story, and continues Maude Meagher’s Maya historical serial with accompanying historical notes. The section closes with the beginning of Era Zistel’s account of two orphaned raccoons, Hansel and Gretel.

subfiles.title: One-Armed Sailor
subfiles.about: Joe Mikkelsson discovers that his one-armed Finnish traveling companion is a fugitive Nazi colonel seeking to recover a key to hidden documents.
subfiles.summary: Joe accepts a ride-sharing companion calling himself Paavo Murto, who repeatedly attempts to kill him in a sauna, on the Oulujoki rapids and at gunpoint. After escaping at Sortavala, the man attacks his former orderly at Olavinlinna in an effort to recover a leather bag containing a vault key linked to incriminating Nazi papers. Joe rescues Hans Fischer, captures the attacker—revealed as Colonel Fritz Meyerhold—and drives both men toward Helsinki to surrender Meyerhold to Allied authorities.

subfiles.title: Metal Mirrors of Aranmula
subfiles.about: The article describes the traditions, manufacture and religious significance of Aranmula’s cast-metal mirrors.
subfiles.summary: Metal Mirrors of Aranmula: Kannan metalworkers legendarily discovered the copper-tin alloy making a ritual crown; local patronage made it an auspicious Hindu object; two families keep the alloy secret.

subfiles.title: An Indian Holy Man
subfiles.about: A full-page photograph depicts an Indian holy man as part of the magazine’s South India feature.
subfiles.summary: Full-page portrait captioned 'An Indian Holy Man'.

subfiles.title: Our Atmosphere: Air…Sea Level and Up
subfiles.about: The article introduces the composition, pressure, layers and temperature structure of Earth’s atmosphere.
subfiles.summary: Popular science article on air pressure, gases, and falling density and temperature with altitude, the troposphere and stratosphere, ozone, cosmic dust, high-temperature regions found by rockets, and volcanic dust.

subfiles.title: Letters to the Editor: World Youth’s Pen Friends Write in From Many Countries
subfiles.from: Rosamond Coolidge; Mary Jones; Viola P. Day; Betty Lampson
subfiles.about: Readers praise the magazine, seek pen pals, submit a story and ask how to send aid to a French family.
subfiles.summary: Letters to the Editor: Belmont Day School keeps the magazine, a girl wants an African or South American correspondent, a burro story, and the editor recommends a ten-dollar CARE package for a French pen pal's family.

subfiles.title: The Little Burro That Went to School
subfiles.about: A prospector recalls Mike, an unusually intelligent burro who returned to a town school at the start of every term.
subfiles.summary: The Little Burro That Went to School: Mike steals pancakes, remembers old trails, and every September goes to the local school to trade rides for food; the narrator is sure he will keep reporting.

subfiles.title: The Rattlesnake God: Chapter Eight—Uxmal
subfiles.about: Teosinte and Chac flee Chichén Itzá for Uxmal, where a high priest urges them to abandon rebellion and found a future Itza refuge at Tayasal.
subfiles.summary: An old stilt dancer tells the fugitives that Chichén Itzá’s rulers have suppressed public outrage over Teosinte’s sacrifice, and Chac leads Teo to the more peaceful Maya city of Uxmal. There he reveals plans for an Itza-Xiu revolt against Mayapan and introduces Teo as his bride to Chel Ixchel Xiu. The High Priest Xiu Xib Xiu prophesies civil war, Spanish conquest and the destruction of Maya cities, directing the couple instead to establish Tayasal on Lake Petén. Chac accepts the command, but when they revisit the Sacred Cenote while leaving, Teo again becomes dizzy and begins to fall.

subfiles.title: The Fateful Uudz Katun
subfiles.about: A sidebar outlines the recurring Katun 8 Ahau cycle and associates its returns with major changes in Maya history.
subfiles.summary: Sidebar: the Uudz Katun is a roughly 256-year Maya cycle tied to Chichén Itzá, Hunac Ceel, Mayapan and Tayasal; the next return would begin in 1953.

subfiles.title: The Xiu Family
subfiles.about: A sidebar traces the preservation of the Xiu family’s written genealogy from Uxmal’s founder to twentieth-century descendants.
subfiles.summary: Sidebar: an ancient Xiu family record at the Peabody Museum continues through Don Nemesio Xiu, thirty-eighth-generation head, contrasting with destroyed Itza records.

subfiles.title: My Friends: Hansel and Gretel
subfiles.about: The author recounts raising two affectionate orphaned raccoons and describes their food, play, habits and attachment to one another.
subfiles.summary: My Friends: Hansel and Gretel: rescued porcupine-quilled animals raised on milk, playing, swimming and climbing; released to the woods, Hansel returns alone and signals something happened to Gretel.
